heading: WebP Compressor Online for Smaller Website Images
introduction:
Website images play an important role in how visitors experience a page. Product photographs, banners, illustrations and other graphics help people understand products and services. However, large image files can increase page weight and make websites slower to load.

WebP is a modern image format developed for web use. It supports lossy and lossless compression, along with transparency and animation. Many website owners use WebP to prepare images that can be delivered efficiently to visitors.

Even when an image is already saved in WebP format, there may be opportunities to reduce its size further. File Compresser provides a WebP Compressor that lets you re-encode supported still WebP images, compare file sizes and review image quality directly in your browser.

You do not need to install software or upload your photographs to an external server. Your device handles the image processing.

sections.heading: What Is a WebP Compressor?
sections.body:
A WebP compressor is an image optimization tool that changes how a WebP image is encoded to manage its file size.

Depending on the selected settings, the tool can create a smaller image while keeping its original dimensions. It can also help prepare images for different website requirements.

However, compression does not always make an existing WebP image smaller. Many WebP files are already optimized, and further encoding may produce little benefit.
File Compresser checks the actual result. If ordinary same-format compression does not create a smaller suitable file, the original is retained unchanged.

sections.heading: How to Compress WebP Images Online
sections.body:
The WebP compression process is simple and does not require technical experience.

1. Visit the WebP Compressor page.
2. Select a supported WebP image from your device.
3. Wait for the website to validate the image.
4. Choose Balanced, High Quality, Maximum or Target Size.
5. Enable resizing only when different dimensions are required.
6. Start processing.
7. Compare the original and processed file sizes.
8. Check the visual details and transparency.
9. Download the result that suits your needs.

You can process multiple supported images in a queue and review their results separately.

sections.heading: Choose the Right WebP Quality Mode
sections.body: Different images require different compression settings. A product photograph may need more detail than a small decorative graphic.

sections.heading: Balanced
sections.body: Balanced provides a moderate quality and file size trade-off. It can be a suitable starting point when you want to optimize an image without applying the strongest compression.

sections.heading: High Quality
sections.body: High Quality prioritizes visual detail. It may produce a larger file, but it can be useful for photographs where colors, textures and small details matter.

sections.heading: Maximum
sections.body: Maximum uses a stronger compression trade-off to prioritize a smaller output. It is worth checking the final image carefully, particularly when it contains fine details or text.

sections.heading: Target Size
sections.body: Target Size attempts to keep the final image within a selected maximum number of bytes. The tool checks actual output size rather than relying on an estimate. If a suitable result cannot meet the requested limit, it reports that the target was not met.

sections.heading: Why Use WebP for Website Images?
sections.body:
WebP supports different image types and can be useful for modern websites.

Some common applications include:

Product images on ecommerce websites.
Blog photographs and featured images.
Website banners and promotional graphics.
Illustrations and decorative graphics.
Images with transparent backgrounds.
General website photographs.

Choosing WebP is not the only part of image optimization. You should also consider display dimensions, responsive image sizes, image delivery and the actual quality needed on the page.

A large WebP file may still be unnecessarily heavy if its dimensions are much larger than the area where it appears.

sections.heading: Can WebP Preserve Transparency?
sections.body:
Yes. WebP supports transparent areas, making it useful for certain graphics and product images.

When working with a transparent WebP image, inspect the output against both light and dark backgrounds. This helps identify any unwanted edge changes.

File Compresser also prevents JPG output when a transparent source would otherwise need to be flattened. This avoids silently removing the original transparent background.
